name: trezor-crypto
listed_description: Heavily optimized crypto algorithms for embedded
reason: No numeric baseline comparison reachable. The trezor-crypto repo was archived on 2026-05-27, its source removed (only README.md and SECURITY.md remain, pointing to trezor-firmware/crypto), and the README says the 2019 code must not be used. The successor README (trezor-firmware/crypto) repeats 'Heavily optimized cryptography algorithms for embedded devices' with no numbers; crypto/tests/test_speed.c only prints ops/s for trezor-crypto secp256k1 sign/verify (no comparison library) and test_openssl.c is a correctness check against OpenSSL. A web search for trezor-crypto vs libsecp256k1, micro-ecc, OpenSSL or mbedtls found no comparison. Directional claim only; the bundled primitives (ed25519-donna, curve25519-donna, poly1305-donna, BLAKE2) are separate upstream projects.

name: utf8.h
listed_description: Single-header UTF-8 library, designed to mimic C-style string
reason: No performance claim or numbers anywhere reached. The README documents a string.h/strings.h-style API (utf8len, utf8cmp, utf8str and others) and a Unlicense dedication; the repo has only a test directory (no benchmark), and a search of its issues and pull requests for performance, benchmark, slow and faster found only a MSVC compatibility PR (#124) and an early-exit PR (#57) with no figures. A web search for utf8.h versus strlen, strstr or other UTF-8 libraries returned nothing about this project. Design goal is convenience, not speed.

name: utf8proc
listed_description: A clean C library for processing UTF-8 Unicode data.
reason: No claim that utf8proc is faster than anything, and no recorded numbers. The README describes a 'small, clean' normalization/case-folding library with no speed statements. The repo has a bench/ directory (bench.c for utf8proc, icu.c for ICU4C unorm2 NFKC, unistring.c for libunistring, using the eprun Deutsch/Japanese/Korean/Vietnamese test files, built with -O2) but no checked-in results; bench/icu.c notes its own ICU run preallocates a huge output buffer. Issue #12 ('benchmarking/profiling', 2014) only asks for a benchmark against ICU; its page body showed no comments, although a search snippet attributed ICU-faster timings to it (Deutsch 0.00390216 s utf8proc vs 0.00011213 s ICU, unverified snippet only, and in utf8proc's disfavour). Search snippets (pages not opened) say other projects that use utf8proc as a baseline, for example NuC8, and the Ruby utf8_proc gem versus UNF, report it slower, not faster. Directional comparison only and not in its favour.
